mcqs.question: The C–C bond length in benzene is about:
mcqs.explanation: All six bonds are equal at 1.39 Å, between a single (1.54 Å) and a double (1.34 Å) bond, because the π electrons are delocalised.

mcqs.question: The resonance energy of benzene is about:
mcqs.explanation: Expected heat of hydrogenation 85.8 kcal/mol minus the measured 49.8 kcal/mol gives about 36 kcal/mol.

mcqs.question: Which of these is aromatic by Hückel's rule?
mcqs.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion is cyclic, planar and fully conjugated with 6 π electrons (4n+2, n = 1).

mcqs.question: The electrophile in the nitration of benzene is:
mcqs.explanation: Conc. H2SO4 protonates HNO3, which loses water to give the nitronium ion, NO2+.

mcqs.question: Which group is a meta director in electrophilic aromatic substitution?
mcqs.explanation: –NO2 withdraws electrons by –I and –R, so the meta position is the least deactivated.

mcqs.question: In electrophilic substitution, chlorobenzene is:
mcqs.explanation: The –I effect of Cl slows the reaction, but its lone pairs (+R) stabilise attack at ortho and para.

mcqs.question: Benzene and chlorine in sunlight (no catalyst) give:
mcqs.explanation: In sunlight a free-radical addition adds six Cl atoms, giving hexachlorocyclohexane (BHC). With FeCl3 you get substitution instead.

mcqs.question: The insecticidal isomer of BHC (lindane) is the:
mcqs.explanation: Only the γ-isomer, lindane, is strongly insecticidal; it is used as a 1% lotion for scabies and lice.

mcqs.question: Saccharin is made starting from:
mcqs.explanation: Remsen–Fahlberg route: toluene → chlorosulfonic acid → ammonia → KMnO4 oxidation → heat to close the ring.

mcqs.question: Which electrophilic substitution of benzene is reversible?
mcqs.explanation: Heating benzenesulfonic acid with dilute acid or steam removes –SO3H, so it can be used as a blocking group.

mcqs.question: The usual catalyst for Friedel–Crafts alkylation is:
mcqs.explanation: Anhydrous AlCl3, a Lewis acid, pulls the halide off the alkyl halide to form the carbocation electrophile.

mcqs.question: Chloramine-T is mainly used as:
mcqs.explanation: Chloramine-T (sodium N-chloro-p-toluenesulfonamide) releases active chlorine; it is an antiseptic and disinfects water.

mcqs.question: Which compound releases CO2 from sodium bicarbonate solution?
mcqs.explanation: Benzoic acid (pKa 4.2) is stronger than carbonic acid; phenol (pKa 10) is too weak to react with NaHCO3.

mcqs.question: The strongest acid among these is:
mcqs.explanation: Picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol, pKa about 0.4) has three –NO2 groups spreading the negative charge of the phenoxide ion.

mcqs.question: Sodium phenoxide heated with CO2 under pressure gives salicylic acid. This is the:
mcqs.explanation: The Kolbe–Schmidt reaction gives salicylic acid, the starting material for aspirin.

mcqs.question: Diazotisation of aniline is carried out at:
mcqs.explanation: Above about 5 °C the diazonium salt loses N2 and turns into phenol.

mcqs.question: A diazonium salt warmed with CuCN gives:
mcqs.explanation: This is the Sandmeyer reaction: CuCl, CuBr and CuCN give ArCl, ArBr and ArCN.

mcqs.question: Fluorobenzene is best made from a diazonium salt by the:
mcqs.explanation: In the Balz–Schiemann reaction the diazonium fluoroborate (from HBF4) is heated to give ArF.

mcqs.question: Phenol, chloroform and NaOH give mainly:
mcqs.explanation: This is the Reimer–Tiemann reaction; dichlorocarbene attacks the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde.

mcqs.question: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because:
options: It has no lone pair on nitrogen
The ring donates electrons to nitrogen
Its lone pair is delocalised into the ring
mcqs.explanation: The nitrogen lone pair is shared with the benzene ring, so it is less available to take a proton (pKb 9.4 vs 4.75).

mcqs.question: Which of these is the strongest acid?
mcqs.explanation: Ortho effect: almost any ortho group makes benzoic acid stronger, even an electron-donating –CH3.

mcqs.question: Azo coupling of a diazonium salt with phenol works best in:
mcqs.explanation: In mild alkali phenol forms the more reactive phenoxide ion, while the diazonium ion still survives.

mcqs.question: Liebermann's nitroso test is given by:
mcqs.explanation: Phenol with NaNO2 and conc. H2SO4 gives a deep green or blue colour that turns red on dilution and blue again with NaOH.

mcqs.question: Saponification value is the number of milligrams of KOH needed to:
options: Neutralise the free fatty acids in 1 g of fat
Neutralise the volatile acids from 5 g of fat
React with the iodine taken up by 1 g of fat
mcqs.explanation: It covers free and combined (ester) acids, so it reflects the average chain length of the fatty acids.

mcqs.question: Acid value is the number of milligrams of KOH needed to neutralise:
options: The free fatty acids in 1 g of fat
All the fatty acids in 1 g of fat
The glycerol in 1 g of fat
The free hydroxyl groups in 1 g of fat
mcqs.explanation: Acid value measures only free fatty acids, so it rises as a fat turns rancid.

mcqs.question: Iodine value of an oil measures its:
mcqs.explanation: Halogen adds across C=C double bonds, so more double bonds means a higher iodine value.

mcqs.question: The reagent used in the Wijs method for iodine value is:
options: Iodine monochloride in glacial acetic acid
mcqs.explanation: Wijs solution is ICl in glacial acetic acid; the excess is estimated with sodium thiosulfate.

mcqs.question: A drying oil has an iodine value of:
mcqs.explanation: Drying oils (e.g. linseed) are highly unsaturated: iodine value above 130.

mcqs.question: Ester value equals:
mcqs.explanation: Saponification value counts free plus combined acids; subtracting the free acids (acid value) leaves the ester part.

mcqs.question: A high Reichert–Meissl value is typical of:
mcqs.explanation: Butter fat has volatile, water-soluble acids such as butyric acid; its RM value is 17–35, other fats are below 1.

mcqs.question: Hardening of oils means:
options: Catalytic hydrogenation of C=C bonds with Ni
mcqs.explanation: Hydrogen is added to the double bonds with a nickel catalyst, turning liquid oil into solid fat such as vanaspati.

mcqs.question: Oxidative rancidity can be slowed by adding:
mcqs.explanation: Antioxidants such as BHT, BHA and vitamin E stop the free-radical chain that oxidises double bonds.

mcqs.question: A very high acetyl value is characteristic of:
mcqs.explanation: Castor oil is rich in ricinoleic acid, which carries a free –OH group that gets acetylated.

mcqs.question: Sulfonation of naphthalene at about 80 °C gives mainly:
mcqs.explanation: At low temperature the faster-forming 1- (α) product dominates; at about 160 °C the more stable 2- (β) product forms.

mcqs.question: Haworth synthesis of naphthalene starts from benzene and:
mcqs.explanation: Friedel–Crafts acylation with succinic anhydride, Clemmensen reduction, ring closure, reduction and dehydrogenation give naphthalene.

mcqs.question: Anthracene undergoes addition and substitution mainly at positions:
mcqs.explanation: Reaction at C9 and C10 leaves two intact benzene rings, so it costs the least resonance energy.

mcqs.question: The resonance energy of naphthalene is about:
mcqs.explanation: Naphthalene 61, anthracene 84 and phenanthrene 92 kcal/mol.

mcqs.question: Naphthalene has how many π electrons?
mcqs.explanation: Two fused rings with five double bonds give 10 π electrons (4n+2, n = 2).

mcqs.question: The Elbs reaction (pyrolysis of an o-methyl diaryl ketone) is used to prepare:
mcqs.explanation: Heating o-methylbenzophenone-type ketones closes the middle ring of anthracene.

mcqs.question: The Pschorr synthesis is used to prepare:
mcqs.explanation: A diazotised o-amino-α-phenylcinnamic acid cyclises with copper, then decarboxylation gives phenanthrene.

mcqs.question: Gomberg prepared the first stable free radical, which was:
mcqs.explanation: Trityl chloride with zinc or silver gives (C6H5)3C•; the odd electron is spread over three rings.

mcqs.question: The anti-inflammatory drug naproxen contains which ring system?
mcqs.explanation: Naproxen is a methoxy-naphthalene propionic acid.

mcqs.question: Oxidation of phenanthrene with chromic acid gives:
mcqs.explanation: C9 and C10 are the reactive positions, so oxidation there gives 9,10-phenanthraquinone.

mcqs.question: According to Baeyer, the angle deviation per bond in cyclopropane is:
mcqs.explanation: (109°28′ − 60°)/2 = 24°44′. Cyclobutane is 9°44′ and cyclopentane 0°44′.

mcqs.question: Baeyer's strain theory predicted the most stable ring to be:
mcqs.explanation: Its planar angle (108°) is closest to 109°28′. In reality cyclohexane is the most stable because it is not planar.

mcqs.question: The most stable conformation of cyclohexane is the:
mcqs.explanation: In the chair all angles are about 109.5° and all C–H bonds are staggered, so there is no angle or torsional strain.

mcqs.question: Bent ('banana') bonds in cyclopropane were proposed by:
mcqs.explanation: The orbitals overlap outside the line joining the nuclei, giving weaker, bent bonds and less strain than Baeyer predicted.

mcqs.question: Freund's method makes cyclopropane from 1,3-dibromopropane and:
mcqs.explanation: Zinc (or sodium) removes both bromine atoms and joins the two end carbons.

mcqs.question: In the Simmons–Smith reaction an alkene reacts with:
mcqs.explanation: CH2I2 with a zinc–copper couple forms a carbenoid that adds CH2 across the double bond, giving a cyclopropane.

mcqs.question: In methylcyclohexane the methyl group mainly occupies the:
mcqs.explanation: An axial methyl suffers 1,3-diaxial interactions, so about 95% of molecules have it equatorial.

mcqs.question: The energy of the boat form of cyclohexane is about how much higher than the chair?
mcqs.explanation: The boat has eclipsed bonds and flagpole crowding, about 6.9 kcal/mol above the chair.

mcqs.question: Cyclopropane reacts with bromine to give:
mcqs.explanation: The strained ring opens, so bromine adds across it to give 1,3-dibromopropane.

mcqs.question: The Sachse–Mohr theory explains that large rings are:
mcqs.explanation: Rings of six or more carbons pucker so every angle stays near 109°28′; decalin's two forms support this.

mcqs.question: How many axial C–H bonds does chair cyclohexane have?
mcqs.explanation: Six bonds are axial and six equatorial; a ring flip swaps them.
